units.text: INT. NIGHT BUS 41 - MOVING - NIGHT
SERIES OF SHOTS:
-- Rain on the window.
City lights smear into gold stripes.
-- CLOSE ON a bus card tapping the reader.
BEEP.
-- ANGLE ON the back rows.
Nearly empty.
A bag of fries going cold.
MIRA, 16, backpack in her lap, sits near the middle.
Across the aisle, HOODIE GUY, 40s, hood up, face turned to the window.
He has been there since the depot.
She digs out her phone.
Dials.
Dad? It's me. I'm on the 41. I know it's late. (glances around) Yeah, I'm okay. I just. I needed to go somewhere.
units.name: MIRA

units.text: Where are you going, Mira?
units.name: TEODOR

units.text: Aunt Lena's. She said I could come anytime. (a breath) You weren't going to let me leave, so I didn't tell you.
units.name: MIRA
paren: pressing her forehead to the glass

units.text: I'm not mad.
units.name: TEODOR

units.text: You are. You're doing the voice.
units.name: MIRA

units.text: -- WE SEE the Hoodie Guy's shoulders tighten.
He does not turn.
-- INSERT: a cracked phone screen on his knee.
It lights up: "MIRA CALLING?" no, "DAD HOME".
It is silent.
He sets it face down.
Tell me which stop. I'll pick you up. We don't have to talk.
units.name: TEODOR

units.text: You'd just stand there with the car running, Dad. You'd say nothing for forty minutes.
units.name: MIRA

units.text: That's, that's not --
units.name: TEODOR

units.text: It is! It's what you do! Mom left and you said nothing, I got in your car and you said nothing, I said I hated you and you said NOTHING!
units.name: MIRA

units.text: Heads on the bus lift.
The Hoodie Guy pushes his hood back.
Gray stubble, red eyes.
Her phone is still at her ear.
His mouth moves on the same words as the voice in the speaker.
I'm sorry, Mira.
units.name: TEODOR
paren: and across the aisle, aloud, the same sentence

units.text: BACK TO SCENE: Mira slowly lowers the phone.
The call timer ticks.
The bus HISSES to a stop.
Dad?
units.name: MIRA

units.text: Say it again. Say it all again, to my face, while I'm standing here.
units.name: TEODOR
paren: standing in the aisle, hands open, voice thick

units.text: The doors fold open on the rain.
Neither of them moves.
